title: Bracket closure and differential compatibility for matrix group schemes
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, let $V$ and $M$ be finite-dimensional $k$-vector spaces, and let $G$ be a finite-type closed subgroup scheme of $\operatorname{GL}(V)$, so that for a commutative $k$-algebra $R$, $G(R)$ is the set of matrices in $\operatorname{GL}(V\otimes_kR)$ satisfying the defining equations of $G$. Put

$$
\mathfrak g=\{X\in\operatorname{End}_k(V):1+\varepsilon X\in G(k[\varepsilon]/\varepsilon^2)\}.
$$

Then $\mathfrak g$ is a $k$-linear subspace of $\operatorname{End}_k(V)$ closed under the commutator $[X,Y]=XY-YX$, hence a Lie subalgebra of $\operatorname{End}_k(V)$ in the sense of [def-wf-lie-algebra]. Moreover, if $r:G\to\operatorname{GL}(M)$ is a homomorphism of $k$-group schemes (a rational representation in the sense of [def-wf-algebraic-representations]), and $dr:\mathfrak g\to\operatorname{End}_k(M)$ is the map with $r(1+\varepsilon X)=1+\varepsilon\,dr(X)$ in $\operatorname{GL}(M)(k[\varepsilon]/\varepsilon^2)$, then $dr$ is $k$-linear and

$$
dr([X,Y])=dr(X)dr(Y)-dr(Y)dr(X)\qquad(X,Y\in\mathfrak g).
$$

That is, $dr$ is a Lie representation of $\mathfrak g$ on $M$ in the sense of [def-wf-lie-algebra].

proof.text: The set g is a k-linear subspace. It contains 0, since 1 is the identity of G(k[\varepsilon]/\varepsilon^2). For X,Y in g, since \varepsilon^2=0 one has (1+\varepsilon X)(1+\varepsilon Y)=1+\varepsilon(X+Y), a product of two elements of the group G(k[\varepsilon]/\varepsilon^2), so X+Y is in g. For a in k, the k-algebra endomorphism of k[\varepsilon]/\varepsilon^2 given by \varepsilon\mapsto a\varepsilon maps G(k[\varepsilon]/\varepsilon^2) to itself (G(R) is cut out by the defining equations, which are preserved under k-algebra maps) and sends 1+\varepsilon X to 1+\varepsilon aX, so aX is in g.

proof.text: For tangent vectors X and Y, the commutator of their two-parameter infinitesimal points is a G-point and its εδ coefficient is XY−YX. Thus XY−YX is again tangent, so the subspace is closed under the commutator.

proof.text: The commutator on End_k(V) is bilinear, alternating, and satisfies Jacobi by direct expansion and reassociation in the associative algebra End_k(V). Therefore the closed subspace is a Lie subalgebra in the sense of [def-wf-lie-algebra].

source.place: Chapter 10, Lie algebra of a closed matrix subgroup

proof.text: Since r is a morphism of k-group schemes [def-wf-algebraic-representations], it gives group homomorphisms r_R:G(R)\to GL(M\otimes_kR) natural in the k-algebra R. Linearity of dr: by naturality along \varepsilon\mapsto a\varepsilon, r(1+\varepsilon aX)=1+\varepsilon a\,dr(X), so dr(aX)=a\,dr(X); and r(1+\varepsilon(X+Y))=r(1+\varepsilon X)r(1+\varepsilon Y)=1+\varepsilon(dr(X)+dr(Y)), so dr(X+Y)=dr(X)+dr(Y). Bracket: with A=k[\varepsilon,\delta]/(\varepsilon^2,\delta^2), naturality along the two inclusions k[\varepsilon]\to A, k[\delta]\to A gives r_A(1+\varepsilon X)=1+\varepsilon\,dr(X) and r_A(1+\delta Y)=1+\delta\,dr(Y). Since r_A is a homomorphism, r_A maps the commutator of [lem-wf-mixed-commutator-tangent] for (G,X,Y) to the commutator of 1+\varepsilon\,dr(X) and 1+\delta\,dr(Y), which by [lem-wf-mixed-commutator-tangent] applied to GL(M)\subseteq GL(M) equals 1+\varepsilon\delta(dr(X)dr(Y)-dr(Y)dr(X)). On the other hand the first commutator is the image of 1+\eta[X,Y]\in G(k[\eta]/\eta^2) under \eta\mapsto\varepsilon\delta, so by naturality its r_A-image is 1+\varepsilon\delta\,dr([X,Y]). Comparing \varepsilon\delta-coefficients gives dr([X,Y])=dr(X)dr(Y)-dr(Y)dr(X).
By the commutator definition on End_k(M), [dr(X),dr(Y)] = dr(X)dr(Y)−dr(Y)dr(X), yielding the displayed formula and the Lie-representation assertion.
